The key distinction is that battery capacity determines runtime, while inverter wattage determines whether the power station can operate your mini-split.

For running a **mini-split air conditioner or heat pump for the most hours**, you want a portable power station with the largest usable battery capacity (Wh or kWh), enough continuous AC output, and ideally expandable batteries.

The key distinction is that **battery capacity determines runtime**, while inverter wattage determines whether the power station can operate your mini-split.

For example, assuming 85% usable AC energy:

| Battery capacity | Mini-split at 500W | Mini-split at 1,000W |
|---|---|---|
| 4 kWh | 6.8 hours | 3.4 hours |
| 8 kWh | 13.6 hours | 6.8 hours |
| 12 kWh | 20.4 hours | 10.2 hours |
| 20 kWh | 34 hours | 17 hours |
| 30 kWh | 51 hours | 25.5 hours |

Actual runtime depends on your mini-split's average consumption, which changes with outdoor temperature, thermostat setting, insulation, and compressor speed.
